title: Controv. IX: Perseverance of the truly just — uncertain necessity, and possible total final fall from grace and faith
pass_a_gloss: IX. On the perseverance of the truly just, of the regenerate (after they have once been justified by faith and placed in the state of grace), as if it were not certain or necessary, and on the possible defection of those same persons from grace and faith, and that total and final, and hence from salvation: the controversy with the Arminians, Article V, pages 257, 258, seems to return. See also the Controversy with the Socinians, LXI, pages 219, 220. Yet we do not confuse the Lutheran brethren with those parties.
pass_b_english: IX. Next comes perseverance of the truly just — regenerate people once justified by faith and already set in grace — treated as if that standing were neither sure nor necessary, and as if the same people could leave grace and faith altogether and for good, and so lose salvation.
At that point the Arminian dispute, Article V (pages 257–258), seems to reappear.
Compare also the Socinian controversy, LXI (pages 219–220).
Even so, we refuse to lump the Lutheran brethren in with those camps.
source_text: IX. De Perseverantia vere justorum, regenitorum (postquam semel justificati per fidem, & in statu Gratiae positi sunt) tanquam non certa aut necessaria, deque possibili eorum defectione a gratia & fide, eademque totali & finali, hinc & salute; videtur redire Controversia cum Arminian. Art. V. pag. 257. 258. Vide & Controv. cum Socinian. LXI. p. 219. 220. Nec tamen Lutheranos Fratres cum istis confundimus.
notes: Controv. print p. 56 / PDF ~157. Opening of Controv. IX before discriminations.

choices.english: as if that perseverance were not certain or necessary
